item.title: Gencom comes for NYC’s luxury hotel crown
item.description: Gencom planted another flag along Central Park South. The Miami-based investor paid about $320 million for the 253-key Ritz-Carlton Central Park South at 50 Central Park South, adding a third Manhattan hotel to a rapidly expanding local portfolio. Property records show a $270 million transfer price, though that figure excludes fixtures and other non-real estate assets. item.title: Richard A.C. Coles on Vanbarton’s office conversion frenzy
item.description: Vanbarton Group’s Richard A.C. Coles is in the running to be the king of New York City’s residential conversions. The developer has converted the drab office building in the Financial District at 160 Water Street into sleek luxury apartments. The firm has three more New York City office projects underway at 77 Water Street, 1011 First Avenue and 6 East 43rd Street. It has another one in Seattle. item.title: Arker, L+M joint venture buy Staten Island complex for $365M
item.description: A joint venture featuring a trio of prominent real estate companies took a break from the cold snap to snap up a large Staten Island apartment complex. Arker Companies, L+M Development Partners and LIHC Investment Group acquired the Park Hill Apartments complex in three separate transactions for a total of $364.7 million, Crain’s reported. item.description: Developers Victor Sigoura and Genghis Hadi landed a buyer for the penthouse at their Upper East Side project, asking $89.5 million. item.title: Affinius-led group to take Veris private in $3.4B deal
item.description: Veris Residential is going private. The Jersey City-based multifamily landlord agreed to be acquired by an investor consortium led by Affinius Capital, alongside Vista Hill Partners, in an all-cash deal valued at $3.4 billion, including debt. The $19-per-share price represents a 23 percent premium to the company’s unaffected share price earlier this month. item.title: Wildflower flips Queens warehouse for $92M
item.description: Wildflower sold a Queens warehouse for a hefty premium. Adam Gordon’s development firm sold the property at 28-10 Whitestone Expressway to Terreno Realty for $92 million, the Commercial Observer reported. The sale comes 12 months after Wildflower acquired the property for $35 million. The property, a former distribution center for the New York Times, is being transformed into an e-commerce logistics center. item.title: Senior lenders move to foreclose on Worldwide Plaza
item.description: The senior lenders behind Worldwide Plaza filed a foreclosure lawsuit, adding another layer to the high-stakes legal fight over the Midtown office tower. Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank and a trustee for the CMBS bondholders allege that owners SL Green and RXR defaulted on $940 million in senior debt tied to 825 Eighth Avenue, according to a complaint filed on Feb. 21 in New York Supreme Court. item.title: Seagram liquor heir rents Soho penthouse for $120K a month
item.description: A Soho penthouse owned by the heir to the Seagram liquor fortune snagged a tenant for $120,000 a month, The Real Deal has learned. Eli Bronfman agreed to lease his sprawling triplex at 20 Greene Street for a year, according to Serhant’s Marc Riedel, who represented Bronfman in the rental deal. Bronfman and his brother, Jeremy Bronfman, also founded California-based affordable housing development firm, Lincoln Avenue Capital. item.title: New Yorker Hotel takeover artist pleads guilty to fraud
item.description: The man who once claimed to own the New Yorker Hotel has something else in his pocket these days: a conviction. Mickey Barreto pleaded guilty to a fraud charge last week, the Associated Press reported, confessing to forging property records to take ownership of the property at 481 Eighth Avenue in Hell’s Kitchen, Manhattan.
